page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c4g1.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance from the ecs.gn5 family, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The server features 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.5 GB per core, and includes a bundled 472 GB local SSD. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU equipped with 16 GB of VRAM. Networking is supported by a 3 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. Traditional compute metrics are low, with stress-ng single-core performance in the bottom 10% and multi-core performance in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large-block read and write speeds falling into the bottom 10%. However, the integrated NVIDIA P100 GPU delivers top-tier performance for large language model (LLM) inference. Prompt processing for both 135M and 7B models ranks in the top 10%, achieving 9863.53 tokens/second and 316.25 tokens/second respectively, while 7B model text generation also reaches top-tier speeds at 42.76 tokens/second.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its reliance on older Intel Broadwell CPU architecture and slower memory subsystems, which limits its effectiveness for general-purpose or CPU-heavy applications. However, the inclusion of dedicated GPU hardware and local SSD storage makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for specialized workloads. It is best suited for small-to-medium LLM inference, machine learning model evaluation, and GPU-accelerated data processing where CPU performance is not the primary bottleneck.
